items.stem: In a right-angled triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
options: The side opposite the right angle
The side next to the right angle
items.answer: The side opposite the right angle
items.markingKey: The hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the 90° angle.

items.stem: Explain how you can tell whether a triangle with sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm is right-angled.
items.answer: Check whether the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15², so it is right-angled.
items.markingKey: M1 compares 9² + 12² with 15²; A1 equal, so right-angled [2]

items.stem: Explain why the hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right-angled triangle.
items.answer: c² = a² + b² is greater than a² and greater than b², since both squares are positive, so c is greater than a and b.
items.markingKey: B1 c² = a² + b² > a², b²; B1 so c is longest [2]

items.stem: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90°, PR = 13 cm and PQ = 12 cm. Calculate QR.

A cuboid-shaped fish tank measures 12 cm by 11 cm by 4 cm. Calculate the length of the longest straight rod that can fit inside it, correct to 3 significant figures.

(a) Calculate the length of the longest straight line that can be drawn inside the box, from a bottom corner to the opposite top corner. (b) Decide whether a thin rod of length 58 cm will fit inside the box. Show your working.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 √(42² + 38² + 20²); A1 60.1 [2] (b) M1 compares 58 with space diagonal 60.1; A1 fits [2]

items.stem: A roof truss for a house in Seoul is in the shape of an isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC = 16 m and base BC = 20 m. M is the midpoint of BC. (a) Explain why AM is perpendicular to BC. (b) Calculate the area of triangle ABC. (c) A support runs from M to the midpoint N of AC. Calculate MN.
items.answer: (a) Triangles ABM and ACM are congruent (SSS), so angles AMB and AMC are equal; they add to 180°, so each is 90°. (b) 125 m² (c) 8 m
items.markingKey: (a) B1 congruent triangles or symmetry; B1 angles equal and sum to 180° [2] (b) M1 ½ × 20 × 12.5; A1 125 [2] (c) B1 MN = ½AB = 8 (midpoint theorem) or by coordinates [1]

items.stem: Which equation is Pythagoras' theorem for a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse c?
items.markingKey: The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

items.stem: Explain how Pythagoras' theorem is used twice to find the longest rod that fits inside a cuboid.
items.answer: First find the diagonal of the base from the length and width; then use that diagonal and the height as the shorter sides of a vertical right-angled triangle to find the space diagonal.
items.markingKey: B1 base diagonal; B1 second triangle with height [2]

items.stem: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 10 cm and another side 6 cm. Sofia works out the third side as √(10² + 6²) = 11.7 cm. Explain the mistake and find the correct length.
items.answer: When finding a shorter side the squares must be subtracted: √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm. The answer 11.7 cm is longer than the hypotenuse, which is impossible.
items.markingKey: B1 subtract when finding a shorter side; B1 8 cm [2]

items.stem: A right-angled triangle has two sides of 8 cm and 17 cm. Grace says the third side must be 18.8 cm. Explain why there is another possible answer, and find it.
items.answer: Grace assumed 17 cm is a shorter side. If 17 cm is the hypotenuse, the third side is √(17² − 8²) = 15 cm.
items.markingKey: B1 17 could be the hypotenuse; B1 15 cm [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why the hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right-angled triangle. (b) Explain how you can tell whether a triangle with sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm is right-angled.
items.answer: (a) c² = a² + b² is greater than a² and greater than b², since both squares are positive, so c is greater than a and b. (b) Check whether the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15², so it is right-angled.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 c² = a² + b² > a², b²; B1 so c is longest [2] (b) M1 compares 9² + 12² with 15²; A1 equal, so right-angled [2]

items.stem: Two triangles are similar. Which statement must be true?
items.markingKey: Similar shapes are enlargements of each other, so angles are unchanged.

items.stem: Explain why showing that two pairs of angles are equal is enough to prove two triangles are similar.
items.answer: The angles of a triangle add to 180°, so the third pair of angles must also be equal; triangles with all corresponding angles equal are similar.
items.markingKey: B1 third angles equal (angle sum 180°); B1 all angles equal so similar [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between similar and congruent triangles.
items.answer: Similar triangles have equal angles and sides in the same ratio (one is an enlargement of the other); congruent triangles are identical, with equal sides as well (scale factor 1).
items.markingKey: B1 similar: same shape, sides in proportion; B1 congruent: same shape and size [2]

items.answer: (a) Angle BAX = angle CDX and angle ABX = angle DCX (alternate angles, AB ∥ CD); angles AXB and DXC are vertically opposite, so all angles are equal. (b) 5/2 (c) 30 cm

Explain why two rectangles are not necessarily similar.
items.answer: All their angles are 90°, but the ratio of length to width can differ (for example 2 cm by 1 cm and 3 cm by 1 cm), so the sides need not be in proportion.
items.markingKey: B1 angles equal is not enough; B1 sides not in same ratio, with example [2]

items.stem: In triangle ABC, DE is parallel to BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 3 cm, DB = 5 cm and DE = 5 cm. Ravi writes BC = 5 × 5/3 = 8.333333 cm. Explain the mistake and find BC.
items.answer: The scale factor compares AB with AD, and AB = 3 + 5 = 8, not DB. BC = 5 × 8/3 = 13.333333 cm.
items.markingKey: B1 must use AB = 8; B1 BC = 13.333333 cm [2]

items.stem: Triangle X has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Triangle Y has sides 9 cm, 11 cm and 13 cm. Kwame says the triangles are similar because every side has increased by 3 cm. Explain why Kwame is wrong.
items.answer: Similar shapes need sides in the same ratio, not the same difference: 9/6 = 1.50 but 13/10 = 1.30, so the triangles are not similar.
items.markingKey: B1 ratios must be equal; B1 shows two different ratios [2]

items.markingKey: Area ratio is the square of the length ratio.

items.stem: Explain why, if the lengths of a shape are multiplied by k, its area is multiplied by k².
items.answer: Area is found by multiplying two lengths together, and each is multiplied by k, so the area is multiplied by k × k = k².
items.markingKey: B1 area uses two lengths; B1 k × k = k² [2]

items.stem: Explain why two cylinders with the same height but different radii are not similar.
items.answer: For similarity every length must be multiplied by the same scale factor; here the radius changes but the height does not.
items.markingKey: B1 all lengths must be scaled; B1 height unchanged [2]

items.stem: A company in Jakarta makes two mathematically similar solid statues from the same metal. The small one is 12 cm tall and the large one is 24 cm tall. (a) Write down the length scale factor from the small one to the large one. (b) Polishing costs $0.05 per cm². Calculate the cost of polishing the large one. (c) Explain why doubling the height of a statue does not simply double its mass.
items.answer: (a) 2 (b) $40.00 (c) Mass depends on volume, and volume is multiplied by 2³ = 8 when every length is doubled.

items.stem: Two similar solids have lengths in the ratio 1 : 2. What is the ratio of their volumes?
items.markingKey: Volume ratio is the cube of the length ratio.

items.stem: Explain why the mass of a solid statue grows much faster than its height when similar statues are made larger.
items.answer: Mass is proportional to volume, which scales by the cube of the length scale factor, whereas height scales only by the factor itself.
items.markingKey: B1 mass ∝ volume; B1 volume factor k³ [2]

items.stem: Two similar shapes have areas 36 cm² and 81 cm². Freya says the length scale factor is 81 ÷ 36 = 9/4. Explain the mistake and give the correct length scale factor.

items.stem: Explain why a diagonal of a rectangle divides it into two congruent triangles.

items.answer: (a) AM = BM and CM = DM (M is the midpoint of both), and angle AMC = angle BMD (vertically opposite), so the triangles are congruent (SAS). (b) Angle MAC = angle MBD (corresponding angles of congruent triangles); these are alternate angles, so AC ∥ DB.

items.stem: At the same time of day in Lagos, a vertical stick of height 1.8 m casts a shadow 2.4 m long and a vertical tower casts a shadow 23 m long. Calculate the height of the tower, correct to 3 significant figures.
items.markingKey: M1 similar triangles: height ÷ shadow equal; M1 1.8 × 23 ÷ 2.4; A1 17.2 m [3]

items.stem: The lines AD and BC cross at X. AB is parallel to CD. AB = 12 cm, CD = 16 cm, AX = 24 cm and CX = 36 cm. (a) Find the scale factor of the enlargement from triangle ABX to triangle DCX. (b) Calculate DX. (c) Calculate BX.
Answer both parts. (a) Two similar shapes have areas in the ratio 16 : 9. What is the ratio of their corresponding lengths? (b) Every length of a solid is doubled. Its surface area is multiplied by
items.markingKey: (a) Take square roots. (b) Area scale factor = 2² = 4.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why the mass of a solid statue grows much faster than its height when similar statues are made larger. (b) Explain why two cylinders with the same height but different radii are not similar.
items.answer: (a) Mass is proportional to volume, which scales by the cube of the length scale factor, whereas height scales only by the factor itself. (b) For similarity every length must be multiplied by the same scale factor; here the radius changes but the height does not.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 mass ∝ volume; B1 volume factor k³ [2] (b) B1 all lengths must be scaled; B1 height unchanged [2]

items.stem: Two similar prisms have heights 6 cm and 9 cm. The volume of the smaller one is 40 cm³. Calculate the volume of the larger one.
items.markingKey: M1 volume factor (3/2)³ = 27/8; A1 135 cm³ [2]

items.stem: A company in Toronto makes two mathematically similar solid statues from the same metal. The small one is 16 cm tall and the large one is 24 cm tall. (a) Write down the length scale factor from the small one to the large one. (b) The surface area of the small one is 280 cm². Calculate the surface area of the large one. (c) Explain why doubling the height of a statue does not simply double its mass.
items.answer: (a) 3/2 (b) 630 cm² (c) Mass depends on volume, and volume is multiplied by 2³ = 8 when every length is doubled.

items.stem: A company in Dubai makes two mathematically similar solid garden ornaments from the same metal. The small one is 12 cm tall and the large one is 20 cm tall. (a) Write down the length scale factor from the small one to the large one. (b) The surface area of the small one is 1530 cm². Calculate the surface area of the large one. (c) The small one has mass 1890 g. Calculate the mass of the large one. (d) Explain why doubling the height of a statue does not simply double its mass.
items.answer: (a) 5/3 (b) 4250 cm² (c) 8750 g (d) Mass depends on volume, and volume is multiplied by 2³ = 8 when every length is doubled.

items.stem: For triangles ABC and PQR, angle A = angle P = 65°, angle B = angle Q = 42° and angle C = angle R = 73°. Decide whether the triangles must be congruent. Give a reason for your answer.
items.answer: Not necessarily: equal angles only show the triangles are similar; no side is known to be equal, so they could be different sizes.
items.markingKey: B1 not necessarily congruent; B1 no equal side, similar only [2]

items.stem: Triangle JKL is congruent to triangle WUV (vertices in corresponding order). JK = 5 cm, KL = 6 cm and angle JKL = 58°. Write down the length of UV and the size of angle WUV.
Triangle JKL is congruent to triangle VUW (vertices in corresponding order). Angle KJL = 35° and angle JKL = 67°. Find angle UWV, giving a reason.
items.markingKey: M1 angle JLK = 180 − 35 − 67 = 78; A1 78°, corresponding angle in congruent triangle [2]
